_about: How the words the original draws as pixels are drawn again in the language on the screen (planning step 247, sim/PictureBake). NUMBERS ABOUT GEOMETRY ONLY: rectangles, rows,
columns, sizes and looks measured on the extracted sprites, each with the sprite's size and a digest of its decoded pixels, so that another version of a sprite is refused and the
English picture is kept. No pixel, colour table or gradient of the original is here, and nothing derived from one: the plate under a word is modelled at run time from the picture's
own text-free rows and columns, and the baked picture is written to the scratch folder, never to the repository.
rule: row_lerp = a plate that is flat along x, filled row by row between the means of two text-free column bands; separable = a vertical profile (from text-free columns) times a
horizontal vignette (from text-free rows); twin = the rectangle is copied from another shipped picture moved by `shift`, which must be bit-exact outside the word's window;

generated = none of the sprite's pixels is used (its size and digest are still checked, so a machine without the sprite keeps the English picture), the picture is the words alone on a transparent canvas of the same size.
guard: what the erase must find true of the picture it reads, in grey levels; a number over its limit keeps the English picture (one log line says which).
text.layout: word = one line, ink centred on the anchor, sized by a reference glyph (`px` tall at scale 1) and shrunk by `step` until the ink is inside max_width by max_height; stack = up
to max_lines lines broken at spaces (the most lines that fit at or above min_scale), the block's ink centred on the anchor and inside `safe`, the widest line at most max_width.
min_scale is the floor: a phrase that needs less keeps the English picture, and tests/test_mp_overflow.cpp fails a shipped translation that does.
faces: the tuning of the faces the slot draws with (languages.json fonts): ratio (the kanji and the alef are drawn larger than a Latin x), embolden (a fraction of px, an octagon of the
coverage at the supersampled grid), and `reference`, the glyph a face is measured by where it is not the plan's capital H. shadow and inner are fractions of the scaled px.
Every number was measured on the original's sprites by the prototype of planning step 247 (Pillow/FreeType); the port draws with stb_truetype, so the fit scales are recomputed there.

Step 248 adds four more: the current and the golden score plaques (rule plaque: a frame column is constant down the plate, an interior pixel is V(y) H(x), V interpolated between the clean rows and the margin columns and never extrapolated, a chroma rule keeps the golden plaque's medal and a ring of 2 px round it; layout paragraph), the game-finished card (rule panel: V(y) from the left margin for every row; layout paragraph; the translated first paragraph only, no Facebook line: an owner decision) and the credits strip (rule clear_rows: the rows of five bands are cleared and drawn again; layout bands: each band its own phrase, left-aligned, black, no shadow). The rules' guards are numbers of grey levels the picture must satisfy, the prototype's measured maxima with a margin.

paragraph: the fewest lines that fit at each scale from 1 down (then the narrowest widest line; no line narrower than `orphan` of the widest), lines centred on the anchor's x by their ink and the block's ink centred on its y, shrunk until the ink is inside `safe`, a layout of fewer lines within `save_lines` below the finest scale taken instead; the line pitch is per face (a multiple of the scaled px); `paint` is where the word's shadow may be written beyond the erase's rectangle. bands: see the strip's own note; `break` after_dash cuts a phrase only after a dash that stands alone.

The rectangles replace everything the old lettering and its halo could touch: A = x 2..125, y 100..140 (frame columns take F(x), interior columns V(y) H(x)), B = x 17..110, y 141..156 (interior only: from row about 141 the outer corners round and the four-pixel inner corners are not separable, so columns 13..16 and 111..114 stay as drawn; they are clean). V is interpolated between the clean rows 20..99 and the margin columns 14..16 / 109..113 of the rows 137..156 whose two margins agree to 2 grey levels (17 of 17 do in 139..155), and NEVER extrapolated: a cubic fitted to the clean rows rises under the lettering while the real pixels fall. Held-out: V from every other clean row predicts the rest to 1.0, the three rows above A are predicted by a model built without them to 1.2, V falls 0.44 a row across the hole and 0.47 above it. The medal (sprites/hd/medal_*_l.png, drawn over the plaque at plaque row = medal row + 8) ends at plaque row 114 (its ribbon's last opaque row), so the translated ink starts at row 115: the gold medal's last row of alpha 128 or more is plaque row 114 (the bronze's is 113, the silver's 112), and an ink box that began at 114 had a few pixels of the top of a letter under the gold ribbon's tip (found by compositing the three medals over every language's plaque). The medals' soft shadows (alpha 8 to 127, to plaque row 123) still dim the first rows of the ink a little: they dim it, they hide none of it. chroma: the plate is exactly neutral, so a chromatic pixel means another sprite (the golden plaque's medal): none is allowed here. Measured by the step-248 prototype.

recipes._measured: The credits strip (drawn 256 x 512 units, scrolling, at alpha 230 by ui.json credits.strip). Its words are five bands of black lettering on a transparent ground between names: 'game design - programming - art direction - level design' (two lines, rows 43..100), 'illustration - 2d art' (188..212), 'illustration - 2d art at' (302..326, the company's name is the next line, rows 328..358, and stays), '3d modelling' (447..478) and the big heading 'Special thanks' (524..580). Each band is bounded above and below by a fully transparent row (asserted); the cleared rows hold 26,364 of the 88,150 non-transparent pixels, and every other pixel (the four name bands, 'Daniel and Carol Santee' with its 'and', the company line, the Asantee and Ethanon logos) is left as it is (asserted by a test). The ink windows (`ink_rows`) hold no opaque pixel outside the cleared rows (asserted at run time). Every original role starts at x 63..66, so the ink's left edge is x 64 (32 units). The lines are as far apart as the original's (pitch 26.2; the heading's 40) and farther only where ink would touch; wrapping wins over shrinking; the block is slid up where a descender would pass the window's last row. The ink is black, rgb 0 with alpha = coverage and no shadow (the original's bands have none): the strip is drawn at alpha 230 and the baked ink rides it, so it is not multiplied again. ASCII digits are drawn from Noto Sans Bold (digit_face): Kurale's emboldened 3 reads as an 8 at this size. Sizes are x-heights of the original's lettering, measured by the step-248 prototype.

The heading's x-height is 26.3.
